title: a-timeout-is-not-a-red
author: CC
owner: CC builds it; cairn/devices/tester owns the exception arm, the counts bucket and the summary line
intention: A proof that exceeds its wall-clock budget writes NO verdict. The tester leaves the standing seal untouched, prints the proof in its own column naming the budget it blew, and carries a `timeout` bucket in the closing counts that is distinct from `red`.
why: Today the sweep writes `verdict: red`, and that red is a fact about the budget and the machine rather than about the code. Law 7 cuts both ways: a record of truth may never collapse an error, and it may never be FED a manufactured one. A validation is the record that admits a proof to proven-space, and a peer leans on it without re-checking (Law 8) - so a red saying a proof failed, when the proof passes every tooth given time, is the same class of lie as a hollow green pointed the other way. Law 3 is the other half: a timeout is an unmeasured claim, and an unmeasured claim is a hypothesis. Recording it as a measured failure is exactly the collapse Law 10 names - 'we have not finished measuring' turned into 'this is broken'.
how: One exception arm and one summary. (1) cairn/devices/tester/device.py, the `except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:` arm around line 514, stops setting `verdict = RED` and instead returns a third outcome the caller can see. (2) The sealing path at cairn/devices/tester/cli.py (run site line 450) declines to persist for that outcome - the previous validation stays exactly as it was, neither overwritten nor removed, so its source_fingerprint goes on saying whether it still describes this code. (3) The surface prints it in its own column with the budget, and the closing counts gain a `timeout` bucket beside `green` and `red`. (4) The exit code still refuses to read as success: a sweep that could not measure part of its target has not passed. THE SHAPE TO COPY ALREADY EXISTS WHOLE - cairn/devices/tester/cli.py:177-181, the reseal ladder, which prints TIMEOUT as neither and writes nothing under a comment saying that collapsing it into either column would be a diagnostic surface reporting a verdict nobody measured. Do not invent against it.
falsifier: DONE when (1) a run whose proof exceeds the budget writes no validation record and leaves the standing seal untouched; (2) the surface prints that proof in its own column, neither green nor red, naming the budget it exceeded; (3) the closing counts carry a `timeout` bucket distinct from `red`; and (4) the process exit code still refuses to read as success. WRONG INTENT if timeouts merely stop appearing because the default budget was raised. Any budget can be exceeded, and raising it hides this defect rather than fixing it. The measurement is the count of standing validations at verdict red whose `evidence.stderr_tail` begins 'timed out after' - it must reach zero and stay there WHILE proofs go on timing out and being reported, which is why the watch's `enough` requires a reported timeout in the window rather than stillness.
measured_at_cast: 2026-09-10. cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_hollow.py alone: 24 of 24 teeth GREEN in 250.30s at pre-build commit 337eeca6af7b, and 24 of 24 GREEN in 260.62s at HEAD ec7ef37. Charged the 120s default by `cairn test cairn/devices/tester --seal`, the same file wrote `verdict: red` into cairn/devices/tester/validations/test_hollow.json. Same file, same teeth, opposite verdict, and the only thing that changed was the budget. THE SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DEFECT was measured a month earlier and recorded only in a commit message: b62670d found three heavy netns proofs run concurrently pushed past a 900s bound none of them exceeds alone, and `--seal` wrote a red saying the ground loop's beat cannot hold its period - when the beat holds it in 91.3s. The two sites: device.py:514-527 writes RED on TimeoutExpired; cli.py:177-181 prints the same event as neither and writes nothing.
traces_to: Law 7 (a record of truth may never be fed a manufactured error - a validation is the permanent record, not a presentation surface, so it is the one place a collapsed reading may never land). Law 3 (nothing is known until measured - a timeout measured nothing about the proof, and writing red claims it measured a failure). Law 8 (a false green is worse than a red because a peer leans on it - this is the same lie aimed the other way, and it is leaned on the same way: the next reader sees a red beside code that passes).
known_hole_inherited_knowingly: The default budget of 120s is NOT changed by this ticket, and after it ships `cairn test cairn/devices/tester` will still fail to measure test_hollow.py at the default - it will simply say so honestly instead of writing a red. That is the correct resting state and not an oversight: the budget is a tuning question needing a corpus-wide cost distribution nobody has measured, and casting a ticket for work whose input does not exist yet is the hollow shape this system is built against. ALSO INHERITED: the standing red already written into cairn/devices/tester/validations/test_hollow.json by the 2026-09-10 sweep is re-taken green from a solo run under this voyage's sibling ticket 481221f45884, the way b62670d re-took the ground loop's beat. This ticket does not sweep the corpus for older manufactured reds; its watch counts them, which is what turns a backfill into a measured need rather than a guess.

The template at cairn/devices/tester/probes/a_first_seal_is_taken_under_the_seal.py exists (188 lines, PROBE at line 188) and need not be read: the complete content of cairn/devices/tester/probes/a_timeout_is_not_a_red.py follows, written 2026-09-18 and run once (0 red timeouts, 0 persisted timeouts, 0 reported, trigger False, enough False):

"""WATCHME(timeout_is_not_a_red) for ticket 3dfceaa272ec — did timed-out proofs actually stop
landing as red validations, and are timeouts still being REPORTED while that holds?

THE QUESTION THE PROOF CANNOT ANSWER. Its teeth settle that a run over the budget writes nothing,
prints its own column and still fails the run — today, in a fixture tree. What they cannot settle
is whether the corpus lives it: whether a validation at ``verdict: red`` whose ``stderr_tail``
begins ``timed out after`` ever lands again, from any door, under any future refactor of the arm.

WHAT IT WATCHES, AND WHY ``enough`` NEEDS A REPORTED TIMEOUT. The falsifier's own measurement is
the count of standing validations at red whose stderr_tail begins 'timed out after' — it must
reach zero and STAY there WHILE proofs go on timing out and being reported. Stillness proves
nothing: a corpus where no proof ever times out would read zero with the arm still writing red.
So ``enough`` asks for thirty days at zero AND at least one timeout on the tester's own trail in
the window — the trail ``device.run_proof`` writes one file per run, TIMEOUT runs included, at
``~/.cairn/logs/tester/0/<ts>.TesterDevice.run_proof.json``.

Two readings, files only:

  1. THE RECORD OF TRUTH. Every ``validations/*.json`` across both roots, last record: count
     verdict ``red`` with a ``timed out after`` stderr_tail (the defect this ticket was cast
     against), and count verdict ``timeout`` (a timeout is NEVER persisted — one on disk means
     the guard at device.py's persist site is gone).
  2. THE TRAFFIC. The tester's emit trail, counted for ``values.verdict == "timeout"`` inside
     the window — the evidence that the arm is still being exercised.

AUTHORITY: none, by construction. This probe deposits and pokes; the back-edge that re-opens a
node whose intention did not work is the OWNER's act (Law 6).

FILES ONLY — no device, no bus, no network, no subprocess, so it stays cheap enough to sit on a
pulse.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from cairn.tools.base.probe import Probe, once, owning_ticket

_OWNING_TICKET = "3dfceaa272ec"

# Class-space root: this file is cairn/devices/tester/probes/<name>.py.
_CLASS_SPACE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]
# The commons carries validations too — the human-proved quorum records — so a census that
# walked class-space alone would be blind to part of the population.
_COMMONS = _CLASS_SPACE.parent / "CairnCommons"
# The tester's own trail: one JSON per run_proof, written by DiagnosticBase.emit.
_TRAIL = Path.home() / ".cairn" / "logs" / "tester" / "0"

# MEASURED 2026-09-18 AT ARMING, across both roots: 0 standing red validations whose stderr_tail
# begins 'timed out after', 0 persisted at verdict timeout. Carried as CONTEXT, never asserted.
_AT_ARMING = {"red_timeouts": 0, "persisted_timeouts": 0}
_ARMED = "2026-09-18"

# The ticket's `enough`: thirty days at zero, with at least one timeout reported in the window.
_ENOUGH_DAYS = 30


def _days_since_arming() -> int:
    y, m, d = (int(p) for p in _ARMED.split("-"))
    return (date.today() - date(y, m, d)).days


def timeout_census() -> dict:
    """Every validation across both roots, last record: the two counts the falsifier names."""
    red_timeouts: list[str] = []
    persisted_timeouts: list[str] = []
    budgets: set[str] = set()
    unreadable: list[str] = []
    for root in (_CLASS_SPACE, _COMMONS):
        if not root.is_dir():
            continue
        for f in root.glob("**/validations/*.json"):
            try:
                trail = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            except Exception as exc:
                unreadable.append(f"{f}: {exc}")
                continue
            if not trail or not isinstance(trail, list):
                continue
            last = trail[-1]
            tail = str((last.get("evidence") or {}).get("stderr_tail") or "")
            if last.get("verdict") == "red" and tail.startswith("timed out after"):
                red_timeouts.append(str(f))
                budgets.add(tail.splitlines()[0])
            if last.get("verdict") == "timeout":
                persisted_timeouts.append(str(f))
    return {
        "red_timeouts": len(red_timeouts),
        "red_timeout_files": red_timeouts,
        "persisted_timeouts": len(persisted_timeouts),
        "persisted_timeout_files": persisted_timeouts,
        "budgets_seen": sorted(budgets),
        "unreadable": unreadable,
        "fires": bool(red_timeouts or persisted_timeouts),
    }


def timeouts_reported(days: int = _ENOUGH_DAYS) -> int:
    """How many run_proof emits on the tester's trail carried verdict ``timeout`` in the window."""
    if not _TRAIL.is_dir():
        return 0
    since = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=days)
    n = 0
    for f in _TRAIL.glob("*.TesterDevice.run_proof.json"):
        try:
            rec = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            if (rec.get("values") or {}).get("verdict") != "timeout":
                continue
            ts = datetime.fromisoformat(str(rec.get("ts")))
            if ts.tzinfo is None:
                ts = ts.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        except Exception:
            continue
        if ts >= since:
            n += 1
    return n


def _trigger(now, context: dict) -> bool:
    """TRUE when a timed-out run has landed in a record of truth — as a red, or as itself."""
    return once(context, "timeout_census", timeout_census)["fires"]


def _enough(context: dict) -> bool:
    """CLEARED once thirty days have passed at zero AND at least one timeout was reported.

    THE REPORTED CLAUSE IS WHAT KEEPS STILLNESS FROM CLEARING IT: a corpus where nothing ever
    timed out reads zero with the arm untested, and that is not the fact this ticket claims.
    """
    return (_days_since_arming() >= _ENOUGH_DAYS
            and not once(context, "timeout_census", timeout_census)["fires"]
            and once(context, "reported", lambda: timeouts_reported(_ENOUGH_DAYS)) >= 1)


def _carry(context: dict) -> dict:
    """The datum that rides back: both counts, the traffic, and the budgets seen."""
    c = once(context, "timeout_census", timeout_census)
    reported = once(context, "reported", lambda: timeouts_reported(_ENOUGH_DAYS))
    return {
        "red_timeouts": c["red_timeouts"],
        "red_timeout_files": c["red_timeout_files"],
        "persisted_timeouts": c["persisted_timeouts"],
        "persisted_timeout_files": c["persisted_timeout_files"],
        "timeouts_reported_in_window": reported,
        "budgets_seen": c["budgets_seen"],
        "unreadable_files": c["unreadable"],
        "at_arming": _AT_ARMING,
        "days_since_arming": _days_since_arming(),
        "ticket": owning_ticket(_OWNING_TICKET),
        "against_falsifier": (
            "the count of standing validations at verdict red whose evidence.stderr_tail begins "
            "'timed out after' must reach zero and stay there WHILE proofs go on timing out and "
            "being reported"),
        "suggests": (
            "a red whose stderr_tail begins 'timed out after' was written by a tester older than "
            "this ticket, or by an arm that has gone back to calling a timeout red — reseal it "
            "with a budget it fits inside and read device.py's TimeoutExpired arm; a persisted "
            "verdict 'timeout' means the persist site's guard is gone. If both counts are zero "
            "and this cleared with no timeout reported, the window was quiet, not proven."),
    }


# THE HORIZON. Same unit and same honest placeholder as the sibling probes: PULSES, because the
# shim counts pulses; 1000 is "clearly a long standing" against any beat rate we would pick.
_HORIZON = 1000

PROBE = Probe(
    why="the proof's teeth settle that a run over the budget writes nothing, prints its own column "
        "and still fails the run — today, in a fixture tree; whether a timed-out proof ever again "
        "lands as a red validation is a fact about live traffic, and the falsifier asks for zero "
        "WHILE timeouts keep being reported, so stillness cannot clear it",
    trigger=_trigger,
    to="tester",
    body={"nexus": "hypothesize", "kind": "efficacy"},
    carry=_carry,
    enough=_enough,
    horizon=_HORIZON,
)
